matt: heads-up: after the kernel-mux tweak landed on canary we see ~18% p99 CPU regression on a tokenization-heavy benchmark. firing perf/flame to get a quick hotspot view.

lee: ugh. which part regressed? tokenization or scheduling?

matt: initial flame shows Python main thread burning in batch_coordinator.handle_batch and a tight loop in kernel_selector::choose_kernel_for_batch (C++). looks like more time spent in Python glue for small batches.

matt: repro steps I used:
```
# start the canary service
./deploy/canary.sh --image=canary-kernel-mux
# run load (short, focused)
wrk -t4 -c200 -d60 http://canary:8080/generate -s scripts/prompt_tokenize.lua
# record perf on the runtime process
sudo perf record -F 99 -g -p $(pgrep redwood-runtime) -- sleep 60
sudo perf script | ./tools/stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded && ./tools/flamegraph.pl out.folded > perf.svg
```

maria: can you paste the top stacks/snippet from perf script? the svg helps but a diffable stack text is easier.

matt: pasted top stacks (trimmed):
```
batch_coordinator.py:handle_batch
  -> batching.py:maybe_flush
  -> tokenization.py:tokenize_batch
    -> tokenizer/_c_tokenizer.so:split_words
    -> PyEval_EvalFrameEx
  -> runtime/kernel_selector.cpp:choose_kernel_for_batch
    -> runtime/kernel_cache.cpp:get_or_compile
    -> open_kernel_impl
```

sam: interesting — choose_kernel_for_batch is C++ but high call count from Python glue. does the mux change increase kernel candidates so get_or_compile does more lookups?

matt: yes, hypothesis: mux now probes both avx2 and sse4 variants per batch and we pay Python-level overhead constructing descriptor objects for each probe. before we cached a single descriptor per model.

perf-bot: perf summary (canary run): 60s sample: top symbols by samples: 1) PyEval_EvalFrameEx 26% 2) choose_kernel_for_batch 14% 3) split_words 9% 4) memcpy 5%

lee: can we confirm batching changed? maybe smaller/purer small-batch distribution -> more probes per token. any traces for batch sizes?

matt: yes, captured a small trace (snippet):
```
[request] seq_len=64, batch_size=1 -> batch_coordinator flushed immediately
[request] seq_len=16, batch_size=1 -> multiple tiny batches
```
seems like the coordinator heuristic now flushes on latency budget per-request rather than building to target batch.

maria: that would explain more kernel selection calls. small batches + kernel candidate probing = bad. can we quick instrument to short-circuit probing when batch_size < X?

sam: suggestion: add fast-path in kernel_selector: if batch_size <= 2 and model_variant==unchanged then return cached_kernel ref without constructing descriptors. minimal change, safe for canary.

matt: added quick patch locally and reran perf: p99 CPU down ~12% from canary but still +6% vs prod. patch diff: https://gist.github.com/matt/abcd1234 (small)

lee: nice. what's the next step? revert mux? or land this fast-path?

matt: prefer landing fast-path first (low risk) and follow up with more robust descriptor caching at C++ layer. also want to add unit that asserts kernel probe count per batch <= 3.

maria: also let's add a flamewatch alert for PyEval_EvalFrameEx above 20% for runtime process on canary/dedicated so we catch regressions earlier.

deploy-bot: canary build canary-kernel-mux-2026 deployed to cluster-canary-3 at 2424242460 :rocket:

sam: action items: @matt land fast-path PR, @maria add flamewatch rule, @lee prepare rollback playbook if fast-path doesn't help on multi-tenant. i'll run a bisect if regression persists.

matt: will open PR in ~1h. attaching perf.svg s3://perf-artifacts/2424242424/perf.svg and folded stacks s3://perf-artifacts/2424242424/out.folded

lee: thanks. also add a small perf benchmark to CI that simulates many tiny batches to prevent future regressions (simple wrk script + perf flame baseline).

maria: noted. I'll add tracemalloc snapshot in the next run to confirm we aren't allocating descriptor objs repeatedly.

matt: quick follow-up after landing fast-path locally: local microbench (1000 reqs) -> kernel_probe_count median dropped from 4 to 1, CPU p99 dropped ~9%. pushing PR now. :thumbsup:
